AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 (monster stream), copied verbatim per governing rule 3 and not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (fabricator.py:120-124). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire. sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion -- the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:2063-2067), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering -- MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) *before* the subclass applies its powers, and `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: this unit's initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power that listens on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7: the four relic files and powers.py cited above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py IS hashed here for other entries); flagged explicitly as the shared finding instructs. ZAPBOT-SPECIFIC ESCALATION CHECK (the shared finding requires one rather than a blind copy, because Zapbot is a MID-COMBAT spawn and not a combat-start monster): Zapbot.cs:29-38 is the only one of the four bots whose AfterAddedToRoom is async and carries a real effect -- PowerCmd.Apply<HighVoltagePower>(ctx, Creature, 2m, Creature, null) after the same TestMode.IsOff visual block the other three have. The sim applies it from __init__, i.e. BEFORE CreatureCmd.add (cmds.py:799-844) puts the bot in combat.enemies, assigns its net_id and rolls its parity Niche HP, whereas C# creates the creature (CreateCreature -> SetUniqueMonsterHpValue, CombatState.cs:232-247), adds it, and only then awaits AfterAddedToRoom (CreatureCmd.cs:68-71). Both inversions are covered by the shared finding's clauses (a) and (b) -- HighVoltagePower's amount is the literal 2 and reads no HP -- and clause (c) holds because Zapbot's initial state is the MoveState 'ZAP', so the constructor roll is a sticky no-op. The one thing the shared finding does NOT cover and this entry adds: Zapbot's __init__ does not read hooks.combat.enemies at all (contrast Fabricator._alive_count), so the not-yet-assigned enemy list cannot bite. The MinionPower the Fabricator then applies (Fabricator.cs:116 / fabricator.py:218) lands AFTER HighVoltage on both sides.
